summary: instagram-bridge: GET /accounts?query= searches Instagram accounts by free text, built early to serve P9's probe.
details: New resource GET /accounts?query= (design/instagram-adoption/16 §Resources, 17 P9/P11), through a new gateway method over instameow's SearchUsers (IGDOmniPickerSearchResultsListQuery, wire name search_messenger_contact_v2), a new domain.AccountSummary entity, and a new app.Service.SearchAccounts use case with the session gate first, same as every other Instagram-facing use case.

The route answers design 16's NEW response conventions from day one, since it has no old body to keep compatible: success is {"items": [...], "next_cursor": null} with no "ok" field; failure is {"error": {"code", "message"}} at 16's full status table (400/404/409/413/500/501/502/503) rather than the older 500-for-everything mapping the other routes still answer. Those routes move onto this table in P14, in the same PR that moves the Python client.

query missing, blank, whitespace-only, or over 64 characters is 400 before any use case runs; both query and username given is 400; username alone is 501 (R-27's unavailable-with-a-reason: GET /accounts?username= is P10's route and its mechanism depends on P9's own result, so it is deliberately not built here).

The result order and count are the library's: no re-ranking, no filtering, no invented paging. A negative test (TestSearchQueryNeverEntersASpan) proves the search query never reaches a span attribute, name, event or status, matching the existing rule for message text; a result count is recorded on the request span instead.
limitations: domain.AccountSummary has no is_private field: slidetypes.SearchResult (the OmniPicker's own wire shape) does not carry it, unlike GetProfile's data.user, which does. Left out rather than invented as an always-false placeholder.
GET /accounts?username= (P10) is not built; it answers 501. Its mechanism depends on P9's probe result, run through this route.
Nora's Python side is untouched: social_fetch's instagram/search stays on OpenCLI until P11's Python half lands (design 17 P11).
